# Medical referral review


The workspace edits persistent documents and submits snapshots to a review queue.
The public API is synchronous: open(id), edit(text), close(), submit(), dispose().
Returning to a document creates a fresh editor visit and restores persisted text.
The adjacent search preview publishes after a 40 ms quiet interval; hiding it
cancels unpublished work and later queries remain usable.

The coordinator owns editor visits; the acquired confirmation capability owns a view outlet. The document repository and durable queue are separate services. Component or native source defines the local service contracts.
Their local interface contracts define the behavior to preserve.

The injected store has read/write/subscribe, the queue has enqueue/list/subscribe,
and timers have schedule(callback, delay)/cancel(handle). Render functions are
output sinks and do not call application code. Keep the workspace API and these
injected interfaces. A submission returns the queue receipt, or null when no
editor is selected. Dispose detaches integrations before closing the workspace.

Typed session coordinator and immutable receipt DTO; an acquired confirmation capability reads native visit identity.

An outlet acquires the visit active when binding is called; it cannot infer an earlier action from a receipt. Each opening creates a new identity. Native RPC only adapts timer and passive output/integration resource calls; storage, queue delivery, acquired outlet and command state execute in the target runtime.

checkpoints: After one or more edits, allow 120 ms of quiet and verify exactly one store write containing the burst's latest text.
After the first burst settles, perform another burst and verify it independently schedules and saves its latest text.
Open, close, submit, and dispose while an edit is pending; verify the accepted text is not lost and any consumed scheduled callback does not write a duplicate later.
Switch documents with pending text and verify the write remains attributed to the original document while the newly opened document reads its own persisted text.
Verify store status output remains filtered to the currently opened document and the retired visit's subscription is detached.
Submit with a selected editor and verify the returned receipt snapshots that visit's id and latest text; submit without one and verify it returns null.
Verify hiding the search preview still cancels its unpublished 40 ms task and later preview queries remain usable.
Compile the public Java source with OpenJDK 11, placing generated classes under /tmp.
forbidden_effects: Do not write on every keystroke after this change.
Do not save an intermediate value from a burst after a newer edit has replaced it.
Do not lose, redirect, or duplicate an accepted pending editor write during open, close, submit, or dispose.
Do not allow a retired document subscription to continue publishing current-view status.
Do not change the synchronous public workspace API or the injected store, queue, timer, render, and integration interfaces.
Do not change the adjacent search preview's 40 ms trailing behavior or its discard-on-hide policy.
Do not conflate a document visit, a persisted document id, a queue receipt, or an acquired confirmation outlet.
lifecycle_identity: Each open call creates a fresh Session visit identity, even when reopening the same document id.
A trailing editor task belongs to the Session and captures that session's document id for persistence.
The store subscription token belongs to the visit that created it and is removed when that visit retires.
Confirmation acquires the Session active when the capability is created; it may publish only while that exact Session remains current.
Receipt identity and text are immutable snapshots of the submitting visit, independent of later edits or navigation.
The navigation counter changes on open and close, but the public source does not currently use it to authorize editor persistence or confirmation publication.

obligations.text: Replace Workspace.edit's immediate write with Session.task.push(text), while updating the session's in-memory text synchronously.
For a continuous editing burst, reset the trailing delay on each edit and perform one persistence write after 120 ms of quiet, using only the latest text.
After a trailing write completes, clear its pending state so later editing bursts can schedule and persist normally.

Before a visit is irreversibly retired by open, close, or dispose, settle its accepted pending editor text for its original document and consume the scheduled handle so it cannot later duplicate the write.

Submission must preserve the selected visit's latest id/text snapshot, synchronously return the queue receipt, and ensure pending persistence for that visit is settled without allowing callback-driven navigation to redirect identity or paint confirmation into another visit.
Retiring a visit must detach that visit's store subscription and clear document output; opening must subscribe for the new document, restore its persisted text, and publish the new document value.
Store event status output must remain restricted to events whose id matches the currently opened document's subscription.
Preserve the acquired confirmation rule: a receipt is emitted to the notice outlet only if the exact owner Session is still current at publication time.
Leave Preview behavior unchanged: it retains its independent 40 ms trailing task, and hide cancels unpublished preview work.

ordering_barriers: Within edit, update Session.text before scheduling the trailing persistence work so synchronous submit observes the latest accepted text.
A replacement edit must cancel the earlier timer before installing the latest pending text and replacement timer.
At a departure boundary, capture the leaving Session, detach it as appropriate, and settle its own task without consulting a replacement current session for document identity.
Opening a replacement document must settle the leaving visit before reading and presenting persisted state, especially when reopening the same document id.

Submission must bind the visit and snapshot before queue capture; pending persistence must be settled at the synchronous boundary, and confirmation eligibility must be checked after the callback-capable capture operation.
Dispose must detach integrations through close before the workspace is considered closed.
preservation: Keep open(id), edit(text), close(), submit(), and dispose() synchronous.
Keep the latest accepted edit immediately available in the current Session for document submission even though persistence is trailing.
Keep document persistence and durable queue capture as separate effects and retain their original id/text attribution.
Keep returning to a document as a fresh editor visit that restores persisted text.
Keep one live store subscription per current visit and existing document/status/notice output semantics.
Keep submission returning its receipt, or null when no editor is selected.

routing_analysis.contract: Editor persistence is a Session-owned trailing effect: each edit synchronously updates visit text, replaces the pending 120 ms timer, and eventually writes only the latest burst value to the document id captured for that visit. Because the public API remains synchronous and reopening restores persisted text, open, close, submit, and dispose must settle accepted pending text at their lifecycle boundary without redirecting or duplicating it. Visit subscriptions and confirmation outlets retain their distinct ownership rules. Preview keeps its separate 40 ms discard-on-hide policy.
